_about: Every APARN meeting. kind: regional (the annual conference) or sar (meetings held alongside SAR). status: held, upcoming, tbc, tba, proposed or announced. Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) where known. Past calls are kept as archive text and must never be shown as open.

events.label: APARN 2019
events.title: The first meeting
events.host: Held with the International Conference on Asia Pacific Arts Studies, Yogyakarta
events.summary: Where it began. Artists and researchers met in Yogyakarta, alongside the International Conference on Asia Pacific Arts Studies, to start a regional network for artistic research.
highlights: Participants: Kurniawan Adi Saputro, Danny Butt, Alison Carroll, Pornrat Damrhung, Léuli Eshrāghi, Michael Hornblow, Khalid Midam and Helly Minarti
Keynote: Gunalan Nadarajan

events.label: APARN2020
events.title: Rebordering the Archipelago: Asia Pacific Exchanges

place.note: Presented by the Centre of Visual Art, University of Melbourne

events.host: Centre of Visual Art (CoVA), University of Melbourne, with APARN. Supported by the Melbourne-Indonesia Research Partnership Program.
events.format: Online panels and conversations over four days, with times in Melbourne and Yogyakarta
events.summary: Four days of conversations about borders, oceans and solidarity across the region, after Édouard Glissant’s line “The entire world is becoming an archipelago.” Speakers included Raqs Media Collective, Léuli Eshrāghi, Yuki Kihara, Natalie King, Nuraini Juliastuti, Sutanto Mendut, Helly Minarti and Mark Teh.
highlights: An open APARN network meeting on 6 November, convened by Danny Butt and Kurniawan Adi Saputro
A First Peoples Research Forum convened by Dr Léuli Eshrāghi (Sāmoa)
A linked postgraduate symposium, Archipelagic Encounters, between LASALLE College of the Arts (Singapore) and the University of Melbourne
Opening remarks by Professor Gunalan Nadarajan, then Dean of the Stamps School
The talks later became the book Rebordering the Archipelago (Perimeter Editions)

programme.item: Raqs Media Collective with Moonis Ahmad, introduced by Dr David Sequeira
Fluid States: Artistic Research in the Great Ocean Basin/Oceania, with Dr Léuli Eshrāghi, Lisa Hilli and Victoria Hunt
Yuki Kihara in conversation with Professor Natalie King
Dr Nuraini Juliastuti and Sutanto Mendut
CoVA/LASALLE postgraduate symposium, Archipelagic Exchanges, with keynotes by Sopheap Pich and Prof. Claire Bishop
Out of the Islands: Four Tangents, convened by Dr Helly Minarti with Tamarra, Ginoe Ojoy, Mark Teh and Iriano Yedija Petrus Awom
APARN network meeting and First Peoples Research Forum

events.archivedCall: The efforts of oppressed peoples to survive in settler-colonial and postcolonial nations build on regional alliances that precede and exceed the colonial imaginary. … APARN 2020 presents a range of panels and presentations as part of a regional exchange of artistic enquiry that can activate regional solidarity in our fields.

events.label: APARN2021
events.title: Graduate Research Meet-up
events.host: Convened from Melbourne and Yogyakarta, on Google Meet
events.format: A half-day online workshop with five-minute introductions to each project
events.summary: The third meeting turned the floor over to graduate researchers. PhD, Masters, Honours and independent researchers each had five minutes to introduce their project, so everyone could see the range of artistic research in the region and find future collaborators.
highlights: Five minutes or 500 words per project, with an optional single slide
Every applicant was invited into the Google Group afterwards

events.label: #APARN2022
events.title: Artistic research for the planet
events.host: Online gathering convened by Kurniawan Adi Saputro, Gunalan Nadarajan and Danny Butt
events.format: 15 short presentations, ending with the inaugural meeting of APARN as a SAR Special Interest Group
events.summary: A day of research on local ecologies, extraction and our responsibilities to the planet, starting from Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak’s “Imperative to Reimagine the Planet”. Presenters came from Thailand, Aotearoa New Zealand, Australia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Austria and beyond.
highlights: Projects from Chiang Rai to Maui: performance remapping, glacial breath, waste research, tropical temporality and mapping extinctions
Ended with the inaugural meeting of APARN as a Special Interest Group of the Society for Artistic Research

events.label: APARN2023
events.title: The Matter of Art
events.format: In person, with 20-minute presentations; creative formats welcome
events.summary: Art results from matter, and results in matter. Artists shared the materials they work with, why that matters to them, and how close attention to material can open our senses to a changing planet.
highlights: Hosted by ISI Yogyakarta, where the network began
Papers published in APARN’s JAR channel: Grounded Methodology Crafting; Encounter ‘Tanah’; No Waste
events.archivedCall: Art results from and results in matter. As art comprehends and works its material, it can transform solid marble into soft and transparent silk, or a disturbance in the air into melodic streams of experience. … APARN2023 invites artists and artistic researchers to share the matter of their practice and why it matters to them and others.

events.label: APARN2024
events.title: Art as Research: Methods for Synthetic Reasoning
events.host: Faculty of Creative Multimedia, Multimedia University (MMU)
events.format: Hybrid: two tracks, twelve panels of 15-minute talks, a panel discussion, an open studio and a closing gig
events.summary: How do we make order and meaning from the world? Two days in Cyberjaya explored art as a way of reasoning: how artworks, as philosophical simulations, produce new knowledge, and how art and technology together can imagine liveable futures.
highlights: Official launch of APARN at MMU by the President and CEO of MMU
Panel on creative practice as research in universities, with Gunalan Nadarajan, Danny Butt and Samantha Jury (University of Hertfordshire), moderated by Yap Sau Bin
Six papers published in APARN’s JAR channel
Live-streamed on YouTube
events.archivedCall: The symposium aims to explore how we create order and meaning from the world around us, encompassing both passive and active forms of reasoning. We invite proposals that explore how art can generate new knowledge, challenge dominant narratives, and envision a better future by engaging with synthetic reasoning methodologies.

events.label: APARN2025
events.title: Artistic Research for Creative Communities
events.host: Department of Dramatic Arts and Faculty of Arts, Chulalongkorn University, with support from its Office of Research Affairs
events.format: In person, with 15-minute talks and 5 minutes of discussion, workshops with local artists, and performances
events.summary: The largest APARN gathering so far, at the Sodsai Pantoomkomol Centre for Dramatic Arts. Researchers, artists and community organisers asked how artistic research can enrich community life, and how communities create new ways of knowing and making.
highlights: Over 150 presentations from 22 countries
Keynote: Arahmaiani Feisal
Proceedings published on the conference website
Papers also invited for Manusya: Journal of Humanities
events.archivedCall: The conference will explore the interplay of innovative approaches to research in and through the arts and the formation of creative communities. It asks for contributions that consider how various modes of artistic research can enrich community life and how communities contribute to new ways of artistic knowing and doing.

events.label: ADPRex × APARN 2026
events.title: Who Speaks? Authorship, Authority, and Authenticity
events.host: Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA), University of the Arts Singapore, with the Arts & Design Practice Research Exchange (ADPRex)
events.format: In person, in the NAFA Studio Theatre and Lee Foundation Theatre: papers, performances, creative interventions and video essays of up to 20 minutes. Free to attend.
events.summary: APARN joined NAFA’s practice-research exchange to ask who speaks through an artwork: questions of voice, authorship and authenticity in collaborative, embodied, traditional and AI-assisted practice.
highlights: Keynotes: Celine Parreñas Shimizu (UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television) and farid rakun (ruangrupa)
Performance: Handle with Care by Ontroerend Goed, arranged with Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay
14 contributions already published in APARN’s JAR channel
events.archivedCall: Encountering an artwork, the question of ‘who speaks’ and whose perspective and viewpoint we are receiving underscores our interaction with what we see, hear, and feel about a piece. … We invite presenters to consider how authorship is shaped and articulated in their work using new (and old) technologies.
